accepts.because: a manifest somebody wants applied. It enters HERE rather than at the submitter because a POST has no sender: the substrate stamps `reply_to` on a CELL's emission, and an operator with a shell is not a cell. This hive lends them one, and the identity that reaches the mutation door is the path of the occupant that served this lane. TWO callers reach it and only one of them is outside the colony: the level above also re-stamps an assistant's `build` / `build_op == 'apply'` onto this lane, so that a colony has ONE submission front door and not two (R-Zielfluss (a)). The level says which by setting `context.operator_caller` to 'agent', and that is the only thing that differs -- the digest, the submitter, the gate and the broker are the same road for both.

produce a dump of a member's memory, asked from the OS side. The lane is named for what the caller WANTS -- a dump -- rather than for the lane it becomes further down: `in_export` is the name the memory accepts, and it is the level below that re-stamps this hive's `export` onto it. Two names because they are two directions, and one name would have made a door and an exit out of the same string

birth, sleep or wake, in the vocabulary the substrate has -- a node born asleep, an edge drawn, an edge cut. It is a lane rather than a second front door because a lifecycle change is a MANIFEST like any other and takes the same road: the submitter, the gate and the broker

a manifest the baumeister DREW for an operator, on its way to a halt rather than to the mutation door (GH #474). It is a lane of this hive and not of the rim: the only sender is the level's own `./builder -> ./operator` edge, which takes the draft of a round that came in at `in_build` and re-stamps it here. What happens on this lane is the opposite of `in_submit` -- the manifest is parked under its own digest in the `drafts` store beside the submission occupant and answered with a receipt naming that digest, and NOTHING is applied. The second act is the operator's own `in_submit` quoting the digest and carrying no manifest. It exists because the builder's contract calls what it emits a PROPOSAL -- `a sentence a human can read before saying yes` -- and between GH #469 and GH #474 that sentence travelled past the human

the broker's answer to the ONE question a submission asks, on its way back to the `submit` occupant inside this hive (GH #556). It is a lane of the FRONT DOOR since the submitter moved in here: the broker stands one level up, beside this hive and not inside it, so the question leaves on `ask` and the answer has to be let back in. This hive reads neither -- it draws two edges and touches nothing. Derived from submit@2.3.0
what the export lane answered, coming back up. Same reasoning as `in_verdict`: this hive asked, so this hive owes the answer to whoever asked it

emits.because: an export request leaving this hive, carrying `hop.target` -- the path of the member whose memory is to be exported. The level below re-stamps it onto the lane the memory accepts (`in_export`) and relays it unchanged from there, which is the same shape this hive's own doors use: a lane says what the caller wants, and the edge that receives it knows where that belongs

what happened, for whoever asked -- a submission's counts, an export's answer, a refusal, or a lane nobody wired. FOUR senders, ONE lane: a caller subscribes to the lane and never to whichever occupant raised it, which is the whole reason a new subject costs an occupant and an edge instead of a change to every caller. It carries `hop.submitter_kind` when the round came in from an assistant rather than from the rim, because the level above has two places to put a receipt and one lane to read it off. The `submit` occupant is NOT a fifth sender: what it raises leaves on `sub_receipt`, because a submission answered twice is a submission whose caller cannot tell which answer is the outcome.

may this identity have a manifest applied under this scope root -- the ONE capability question a submission asks, raised by the `submit` occupant and let out of the front door because the broker is this hive's SIBLING and not its occupant (GH #556). It has exactly one sender in here, which is what lets the level above stamp the requester on the edge that receives it (R-AC-1): the identity the broker rules is `<this hive>/submit`, the node whose reach the rule is about, and never this hive as a whole. Derived from submit@2.3.0

the manifest, checked and attributed, on its way to the mutation door. It crosses this rim since GH #556 and NOTHING about it is this hive's: no cell of the front door raises it, no cell of the front door may, and the edge that finally carries it to `/colony/mutations` lives in the birth topology of the colony's root -- `/colony/mutations` is not an endpoint a mutation may draw at any scope, so the reach cannot be acquired later by anything that happens in here. What moved is where the submitter STANDS, not what it is allowed to do (ADR-0015 § Amendment 2026-08-31). Derived from submit@2.3.0

the SUBMITTER's own receipt, in its own words, for the level above -- and only in the two shapes this hive cannot answer for: one carrying `hop.error_code`, and one whose committed diff registered a template class (`hop.registers_class`). The ordinary committed receipt is rendered for the caller by the occupant that asked and stays inside; letting a copy of it out as well would be one submission with two answers on two lanes. It is a lane of its own rather than a second sender on `receipt` for exactly that reason, and what the level does with it -- GH #504's nudge into the baumeister's corpus, the refusal that closes a drafted round -- is the level's business and not this hive's. Derived from submit@2.3.0

required_drains.because: a caller that hands this hive a manifest and does not take the receipt back has asked for a change to the colony and arranged never to learn whether it happened. A manifest rolls forward with no rollback, so 'I do not know' is the one answer that cannot be recovered from
the same decision, one composition step earlier: a birth, a sleep or a wake becomes a manifest, and a manifest owes its requester an outcome

the whole POINT of the lane is the answer: a draft that is parked and never announced is a manifest nobody was shown, which is the defect GH #474 names with the halt removed instead of added. A level that wires the draft in and the receipt nowhere has built a silence with extra steps
an export that answers into nothing is indistinguishable from one that never ran. The pair is one decision

a composition that wires the broker's answer and not the question -- or the question and not the answer -- has arranged for every submission to hang parked forever, under a digest nobody will ever quote again. The pair is one decision, and it is the submitter's own `required_drains` raised one level: the broker is a sibling of this hive, so the round trip crosses this rim twice and both crossings have to be drawn
the same pair on the export side: a level that subscribes to the answer and never forwards the question has arranged for an answer that can never arrive

edges.condition: has(hop.route) && hop.route != 'export' && hop.route != 'receipt' && hop.route != 'ask' && hop.route != 'mutate' && hop.route != 'sub_receipt'

description.purpose: The colony's front door, and the one place a person addresses it: ONE sealed hive at the OS level with one occupant per subject -- a submission (`intake`), an export, a lifecycle change, and since GH #474 a DRAFT that waits -- reached by naming the lane and never the cell. It decides nothing. What it supplies is the one thing a POST from outside does not have: an IDENTITY, because the substrate stamps the emitting CELL's path as reply_to and an operator with a shell is not a cell. Since GH #556 the SUBMITTER lives here too, as the `submit` occupant: one front, one place a submission lives, and a road that is readable off the graph instead of crossing two stations of the shell for one job. It remembers exactly one thing, and the sentence `it holds nothing` is RETRACTED with GH #474: a manifest the baumeister drew for an operator is parked in `drafts` under its own digest until that operator quotes the digest back. Nothing else is remembered between two requests, and the parked draft is a proposal rather than state a request depends on -- a colony that lost the store would lose offers nobody accepted, never a change it made.
description.use_when: Once per colony, at the OS level, beside the baumeister that drafts and the broker that rules. Draw ONE edge to the hive path per lane, and one back off it on `receipt`. Two of the lanes are not a caller's: `in_draft` is a manifest the level's own `./builder -> ./operator` edge brings, and `in_verdict` is the broker's answer the level's own `./access -> ./operator` edge brings back -- the question left on `ask` one hop earlier. A new subject -- a further thing an operator may ask the OS for -- is an occupant and a door INSIDE this hive; the caller's edges do not move.
description.not_in_scope: No authentication, ever. There is no token here, no header check, no allow-list of callers and no secret: this hive answers WHO the sender is, never WHETHER they are who they say. Who may reach the front door is a reverse proxy's question, and what the holder of an identity may DO is the capability broker's answer. No decision either -- every manifest still travels the digest, the gate and the broker before anything is applied. The sentence `no edge from any cell in here onto the mutation door` is PRECISED rather than dropped with GH #556: the submitter stands in this hive now, so `mutate` crosses this rim -- but no cell of the front door raises it, none may, and the reach itself is unchanged, because `/colony/mutations` is not an endpoint a mutation may draw at any scope. It is birth topology or it does not exist, and it cannot be acquired by anything that happens in here. And no state a request DEPENDS on: the `drafts` store holds proposals nobody has said yes to, and nothing else survives between two requests.
description.contract_in: Six lanes, all at the hive path. in_submit, in_dump and in_lifecycle are what a caller asks for; export_done is the answer to the one of those that still leaves the hive; in_draft is a manifest the baumeister drew for an operator, and its only sender is the level's own `./builder -> ./operator` edge; in_verdict is the broker's answer to the ONE question a submission asks, and its only sender is the level's own `./access -> ./operator` edge. in_submit has two callers -- a person at the rim, and an assistant inside the colony whose apply the level re-stamps onto it -- and `context.operator_caller == 'agent'` is how the level says which. It also takes TWO shapes since GH #474: a manifest in the body, or the digest of a parked draft and no manifest at all. `in_receipt` is NO LONGER a lane of this hive (GH #556): the submitter's answer to `intake` is one edge inside the hive now, and a door for it would be a door nobody outside can reach.
description.contract_out: Five lanes, all out of the hive path. export is a request for the memory that holds the record -- the level below re-stamps it onto `in_export` and relays it from there. receipt is what happened, with FOUR senders and one declaration; a draft that was parked answers on it too, marked `hop.draft_state == 'draft_ready'` and carrying `hop.manifest_sha256` and `hop.draft_path`, and a receipt carries `hop.submitter_kind` back when the round began inside the colony, because the level above sends that one DOWN to the assistant that asked instead of out of the colony. The remaining three arrived with the submitter (GH #556) and none of them is the front door's own: ask is the capability question, raised by `./submit` and answered back in on `in_verdict`; mutate is the checked, attributed manifest on its way to a door that lives in the birth topology of the colony's root; sub_receipt is the submitter's own receipt in its own words, let out ONLY when it carries `hop.error_code` or `hop.registers_class` -- the ordinary committed one is rendered for the caller inside this hive, and a submission with two answers on two lanes is a submission whose caller cannot tell which is the outcome. `apply` is NO LONGER a lane of this hive: it is the edge `./intake -> ./submit`, and it crosses nothing.
